author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it by full name, all on one page. It is reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name on a single page, with no pagination
given a veterinarian holding a specialty, when the specialty page is opened, then that veterinarian's first name and last name appear, in that order (for example "Helen Leary"), under that specialty
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty page is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on it
edge case 1: a veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each of them
edge case 2: a specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian beneath it
edge case 3: a specialty name appears exactly as stored, in every supported language
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged per owner decision)
a navigation entry or a link to the page from any other page (owner decision: reachable by its URL alone; entry point may be a follow-up)
a machine-readable form of the specialty list
a defined order for specialties or for veterinarians under each (recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md)
an explicit 'none' marker for an unheld specialty (recorded as an open question)
notes: Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log. Existing requirements that bind the new page: REQ-SYS-001 (the page carries the shared navigation to owner search and the vet directory; the navigation itself gains no entry), REQ-LANG-002 (any new wording, such as a heading, is present in every supported language, not hard-coded). Specialty names are stored data and are shown untranslated. The file_targets are a best guess, and system-design-expert may revise the template path and the message bundles.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays in the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure) and reuses patterns already in force. A new SpecialtyRepository follows the PetTypeRepository lookup-repository precedent. It supplies every specialty, including unheld ones, which VetRepository.findAll cannot produce. A new package-private SpecialtyController serves GET /specialties.html, one surface per controller as the owner package demonstrates. Holder grouping lives in a new value object, SpecialtyHolders, not in the controller: inverting 'a veterinarian holds specialties' is domain logic (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; Design Principle 4). Adjustments written: Contracts rows for SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyHolders, SpecialtyController, and REQ-VET-003 on Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, CacheConfiguration; one invariant sentence; a new § Scale and Load section with the specialty-page row. Deviation from the prd-entry file_targets: SpecialtyController and SpecialtyControllerTests replace the VetController/VetControllerTests edits, VetRepository is unchanged, and no message bundle changes (the existing 'specialties' and 'vets' keys cover the heading and column). Basis: grep of vet/*.java, owner/PetTypeRepository.java, templates/vets/vetList.html, templates/fragments/layout.html, and messages/*.properties; IDE oracle not connected, so this is the weaker basis.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html (SpecialtyController): binds no request input, with no @RequestParam, no path variable, and no @ModelAttribute. The binding target is none. Model attribute: the List<SpecialtyHolders> built from SpecialtyRepository.findAll() and VetRepository.findAll(). Returns view vets/specialtyList.
SpecialtyRepository: Spring Data Repository<Specialty, Integer> with one @Transactional(readOnly = true) findAll(), uncached. It needs no @Cacheable, so vet-cache Open Question 5 is not widened.
VetRepository.findAll() (the existing cached unpaged read) is reused unchanged; no new VetRepository method.

Template vets/specialtyList.html uses the shared layout (REQ-SYS-001) with a menu argument that matches no nav item, so the nav gains no entry and nothing is highlighted. The heading is #{specialties}, the holder column #{vets}. Each holder renders as vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName, the same expression as vetList.html. Specialty names render with th:text so they stay escaped and untranslated (REQ-LANG-002, edge case 3). There is no pagination block and no 'none' marker.

Double, repository boundary in SpecialtyControllerTests (@WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class) + MockMvc, the sanctioned transport stub): supply hand-written fixed-list implementations of SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository through a @TestConfiguration, preferred per testing-principles § Mocking Policy. A @MockitoBean stub is tolerated only if the hand-written double proves impractical against the cache proxy; record the reason in the test.
Double, none in SpecialtyHoldersTests: a plain unit test over real Specialty and Vet instances, with no Spring context.
Double, real implementation (optional): a SpecialtyRepository.findAll case in the existing @DataJpaTest ClinicServiceTests against H2 seed data (radiology, surgery, dentistry).

patterns.description: Repository for a persisted lookup value, as a standalone read-only Spring Data interface
Read-only transactional Spring Data read; SpecialtyRepository mirrors the annotation but not @Cacheable
Layout fragment usage, table markup, and the full-name expression to reuse

SpecialtyHolders is the first non-entity domain type: a record with the closed properties in full. It holds an immutable List.copyOf of its holders and rejects a null specialty at construction. A static factory builds one per specialty from the two collections

risks.risk: Instance-equality grouping silently drops every holder. BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode, and the cached Vet graph and the fresh SpecialtyRepository result are distinct instances
risks.mitigation: Key the grouping by Specialty id, per the system-design § Contracts invariant sentence and architecture-principles § Domain Core (reference by identity). SpecialtyHoldersTests builds holders' specialties as instances distinct from the listed ones with the same id

risks.risk: Specialty page path scales with specialties and held pairs (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty-page row)
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one pass into an identity-keyed map, then one entry per listed specialty. No new query, index, or cache

risks.risk: Mapping an inverse Specialty-to-vets association instead of a repository creates a Vet-Specialty-Vet cycle in the serialized /vets output and an extra eager fetch
risks.mitigation: Leave Specialty's mapping unchanged; entities are touched only under the scoped persistence-entity exception (architecture-principles § Scoped exception), and this slice needs no entity change

risks.risk: Tests that assert an order, which REQ-VET-003 leaves open (PRD Open Questions)
risks.mitigation: Assert membership under each specialty, not position. The implementation may keep repository order and adds no sorting rule

risks.risk: A business rule creeps into SpecialtyController
risks.mitigation: Controller delegates to SpecialtyHolders' factory and selects the view only (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row)

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log. Five-signal check: no signal trips. The design doc is populated and partly confirmed, framework and architecture-shape ADRs exist, the vocabulary is confirmed, the concerns the slice touches (persistence, i18n) have patterns, and no new bounded context is added. Non-goals checked: NG-2 is honored because the slice is read-only, with no new write path and no cache eviction. No ADR: the one rejected alternative (an inverse association) is contained in this slice and recorded as a risk. Code names use canonical terms only (Specialty; 'holds' is the vocabulary's relationship verb), so no ubiquitous-language entry is needed. Open questions carried from the PRD and not decided here: the entry point, the ordering, and an explicit empty-specialty marker. The § Scale and Load row records the size as 'unrecorded, treated as bounded' pending an owner figure.

findings.location: docs/system-design.md:80 (Invariants paragraph) and docs/system-design.md:127 (Scale and Load, Form column)
findings.description: "matches ... by identity, not by instance" and "identity-keyed map" are ambiguous. In Java, identity means instance identity, which is the opposite of what src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/SpecialtyHolders.java does: it keys a HashMap<Integer, List<Vet>> on the specialty's id (`holdersBySpecialtyId.computeIfAbsent(held.getId(), ...)`). A reader could implement it with an identity map and lose every match, since the vets and specialties are loaded separately and share no instances. The same wording appears in both places.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: New endpoint binds no request input: SpecialtyController.java adds only `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")` with a `Model` parameter; a grep of src/main/java/.../vet/ for @ModelAttribute|@RequestParam|@PathVariable|@RequestBody|@Query matches only the pre-existing `VetController.java:45 public String showVetList(@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page, Model model)`. So no mass-assignment, injection or cross-request-trust surface is added. The exposure is read-only specialty names and veterinarian names that the existing /vets.html page already publishes, which is within the demonstration baseline in docs/security-principles.md (Widening the exposed surface).

Output escaping stays on: specialtyList.html renders stored values only through th:text (`th:text="${entry.specialty.name}"`, `th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}"`), and `grep -rn -F -e 'th:utext' src/main/resources/templates/vets/` returns nothing. The template adds no preprocessing (`__${...}__`). The layout's existing preprocessing (`fragments/layout.html:31 th:href="@{__${link}__}"`) receives only literal links, and the new page passes the fixed literal menu value 'specialties'.
Data access goes through a Spring Data derived `findAll()` on SpecialtyRepository with `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`: no query text, no parameters, least privilege.

Shared cache state is not mutated: SpecialtyHolders only reads cached Vet instances. `Vet.java:60-63` getSpecialties() returns a freshly collected sorted list (`.collect(Collectors.toList())`), and the record's compact constructor copies holders (`List.copyOf`). The HashMap is request-local, so the singleton controller holds no mutable state.

Resource use is linear and matches the bounded, write-path-free data set recorded in system-design.md § Scale and Load. No file I/O, logging, exceptions carrying data, or shell execution is added. A search of the diff finds no hardcoded secrets.

Supply chain: build.gradle is unchanged and the diff adds no dependency. No NVD match ran because OWASP Dependency-Check is not configured (`grep dependencyCheck build.gradle` finds nothing). Resolved runtime versions from `./gradlew dependencies`: Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5, jackson-databind (tools.jackson) 3.1.5.

author: change-grader
summary: add read-only specialty page listing each specialty's holders

blast_radius.note: All production changes are new files in the vet package: a controller mapped to one new unauthenticated GET route that binds no input, a value record, a read-only Spring Data repository, and a template. No existing production code is edited, and no sensitive paths are touched. The doc edits are additive rows and one new Scale and Load section.

semantic_surprise.note: I read the hunks and found nothing surprising. Matching goes by specialty id through a HashMap used only for lookup. Output follows the findAll order of the specialties, and unheld specialties map to an empty list. The template renders names with th:text, which escapes them. The cached, shared Vet instances are only read, never mutated. Vet specialties are EAGER, so open-in-view being off is safe. The specialties and vets message keys exist in every bundle.

test_adequacy.note: The SpecialtyHolders unit tests assert real outcomes and cover each edge case: several specialties per vet, unheld specialties, vets holding none, and id matching against separately loaded copies. The last one is valid because BaseEntity defines no equals. One gap: the page-level test checks that the holder appears somewhere on the page, not beside its own specialty. It also does not check that a vet with no specialty is absent. The unit tests own that pairing.

reviewer_hedging.note: All dispatched reviewers approved. The round-1 test-reviewer approval carried three recommendations that are still open in the final diff. The prd-entry test_names no longer match the tests: coverage-map shows 3 of 5 declared names absent. In ClinicServiceTests, a local variable shadows the new specialties field, and the NamedEntity import is out of order. No page-level test pins a holder to its specialty.

scope_deviation.note: The change stays within the REQ-VET-003 bullets. It adds one unlinked, unpaged, read-only page and nothing else. No consultations, no build retries at the cap (one build failure), and the second design-block was a doc-reviewer autofix wording fix, not a scope revision. The PRD open questions record the owner's no-link decision.

rationale: The code is small, contained, and correct on read, and I found no semantic surprise. The only flag is that the test reviewer approved with recommendations that remain unaddressed: prd-entry test_names drift, a shadowed local in ClinicServiceTests, and no page-level check that holders sit beside their own specialty. Skim the production code and decide whether to fix those before merging.
